campbell.title: Campbell City Council — September 1, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council considered a resolution to authorize a funding agreement with the Santa Clara Valley Transportation Authority for a low-carbon transportation program supporting transit reliability and performance improvements. The agenda also noted an item related to pothole damage claims processes.
keyTopics: Resolution to authorize a fund agreement with the Santa Clara Valley Transportation Authority for the Low-Carbon Transportation and Operations Program
Funding for a transit reliability improvement and performance systems project
Pothole damage claims process

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — September 2, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council reviewed routine items like meeting minutes, vendor payments, and the Treasurer's Report, along with draft responses to two county grand jury reports on pothole damage claims and VTA's oversight of the BART Silicon Valley extension. The Council also considered a transportation impact fee study contract, forming a committee to look into alternative policing services, the future of the Saratoga Blossom Festival, and whether to continue participating in the Cities Association of Santa Clara County.
keyTopics: Draft responses to grand jury reports on pothole damage claims processes and VTA's management of BART Silicon Valley Phase II
Support for AB 1761, a bill on utility data transparency for the Power Charge Indifference Adjustment
An $85,000 contract with Fehr and Peers for a Transportation Impact Fee study
Forming an Ad-Hoc Committee to review alternative policing services in Saratoga
Whether to continue the Saratoga Blossom Festival and the City's involvement in the Cities Association of Santa Clara County

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — September 8, 2026
los-altos.summary: The Los Altos City Council took up routine budget and contract items, including updated pay schedules for city employee groups and additional funding for an electrical maintenance contractor, alongside a proposal to rename Lee Street to Tubman Street. The Council also discussed committee structures, including changes to the Volunteer Awards Committee and the Environmental Commission, plus a citizen initiative on zoning impacts.
keyTopics: Resolution renaming Lee Street to Tubman Street
Revised Fiscal Year 2026/27 pay schedules for city employee associations and unrepresented staff
Amendment adding $250,000 to the maintenance agreement with Bear Electrical Solutions
Disbanding the joint Los Altos-Los Altos Hills Volunteer Awards Committee to form a Los Altos-only version
Citizen initiative presentation on potential impacts to zoning

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — September 1, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council met to approve routine meeting minutes from several August 2026 sessions, and considered a resolution to vacate a public service easement at 15995 Cerro Vista. The Council also took up a resolution to establish preferential and time-limited parking permits, and a consultant agreement related to executive services.
keyTopics: Vacating a public service easement at 15995 Cerro Vista
Establishing preferential permit parking and time-limited parking
Consultant agreement for executive-related services
Approval of minutes from multiple August 2026 Town Council meetings

san-jose.body: Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole
san-jose.title: San José Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole — September 9, 2026
san-jose.summary: The Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole reviewed the upcoming September 15 and September 22, 2026 City Council agendas, including any new items and scheduling needs. The committee also considered routine reports from the City Clerk and City Auditor, a mayoral travel request, and a memo on Council transparency and non-disclosure agreements.
keyTopics: Review and finalization of the September 15, 2026 Council agenda
Review of the September 22, 2026 draft Council agenda
Public Record report for August 27 - September 3, 2026
City Auditor's monthly activity report for August 2026
Council Transparency and Private Non-Disclosure Agreements memo from Council members Ortiz, Campos, Cohen, Candelas, and Casey

mountain-view.title: Mountain View Council Neighborhoods Committee — September 10, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The Mountain View Council Neighborhoods Committee held an open meeting where city staff were available to answer questions from residents about neighborhood issues. Residents were invited to submit questions in advance online or raise other topics during the meeting's open comment period.
keyTopics: City staff Q&A session on neighborhood-related questions
Advance submission of resident questions via an online form
Open oral communications period for any non-agenda topics

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — August 25, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The Sunnyvale City Council held a closed session, received a presentation on the Clean Water Program, and then covered a regular meeting agenda that included library equipment purchasing, a city job classification update, and a Caltrain budget briefing. Council also reviewed progress on its Year 1 strategic workplan.
keyTopics: Clean Water Program update presentation by staff
Purchase order authorization for a new automated materials handling system at the Main Library
New job classifications and title updates for several city positions, plus a labor side letter with the Communication Officer's Association
Update on Caltrain's budget from the Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board
Review of progress on the Council's Year 1 strategic workplan

cupertino.title: Cupertino Teen Commission — September 9, 2026
cupertino.summary: Cupertino's Teen Commission kicked off its new term by swearing in the incoming 2026-2028 commissioners and holding an orientation for them. The Commission also reviewed teen programs, selected its Chair and Vice Chair for 2026-2027, and considered topics for meetings over the coming year.
keyTopics: Swearing-in ceremony for incoming 2026-2028 Teen Commissioners
New commissioner orientation
Presentation on teen programs
Selection of 2026-2027 Chair and Vice Chair
Discussion of Teen Commission meeting topics for 2026-2027

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council — August 25, 2026
santa-clara.summary: The Santa Clara City Council considered an appeal of an approved architectural review permit for a project at Civic Center Drive and Alviso Street that would demolish existing buildings and build 14 townhomes plus a duplex with commercial space. The Council also considered a vesting tentative subdivision map for a 147-unit residential project with one commercial building at Homestead Road, reviewed under state housing law SB 330. Separately, the Council held interviews to appoint two members to the Civil Service Commission.
keyTopics: Appeal of architectural review permit for a 14-townhome and duplex project with commercial space at 860/858 Civic Center Drive and 1526 Alviso Street, with a statutory CEQA exemption determination under AB 130

Vesting tentative subdivision map for 147 units and one commercial building at 3521 and 3591 Homestead Road, considered under SB 330, with CEQA review tied to an adopted Mitigated Negative Declaration
Interviews and appointment of two applicants to the Civil Service Commission

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — September 1, 2026
milpitas.summary: The City Council, acting as the board for the city's former redevelopment agency's Successor Agency, considered administrative and financial housekeeping items. This included confirming which city officials hold Successor Agency officer roles and authorizing the sale of refunding bonds tied to old redevelopment agency debt.
keyTopics: Confirming and designating city officials as officers of the Successor Agency to the Redevelopment Agency
Authorizing issuance and sale of 2026 Tax Allocation Refunding Bonds to refinance existing Successor Agency debt

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto Climate Action and Sustainability Committee — September 4, 2026
palo-alto.summary: Palo Alto's Climate Action and Sustainability Committee reviewed an early look at the city's 2025 greenhouse gas inventory, including a closer look at 'Scope 3' emissions (indirect emissions from things like purchased goods and services). The committee also discussed different approaches the city could take toward its carbon neutrality goal and gave staff feedback on what areas need further analysis.
keyTopics: Preliminary review of the 2025 Greenhouse Gas Inventory
Overview of Scope 3 emissions
Approaches to achieving the city's carbon neutrality goal
Committee feedback on areas for further staff analysis
